title: Immunization Protocol - Entries Taken Off for a Latest Dose Given Too Early
content:
**Immunization Services protocol: the dose found not to count, when a course's valid doses still needed are rebuilt from its dose history.**

**Clause 1.** The dose found not to count is taken off as follows. Where the latest dose on record came too early, meaning dose 2 less than the dose 2 minimum interval less the grace period days after dose 1, or dose 3 less than the dose 3 minimum interval from dose 2 less the grace period days after dose 2 or less than the dose 3 minimum interval from dose 1 less the grace period days after dose 1, and it was recorded from another provider, 1 entry is taken off. Where the latest dose came too early and Kestrel gave it at one of its stores, 2 entries are taken off, the dose and the registry copy of Kestrel's report of it. Where the latest dose did not come too early, no entry is taken off as found.

**Clause 2 (reading the dates).** The latest dose on record is the dose entry on the course with the latest date, and its dose number decides which interval test applies. The date of dose 1 is the date of the dose 1 entry on the course (the latest-dated one where there are several); the date of dose 2 is read the same way. Days are calendar days between the two dose dates. A latest dose that is dose 1 never came too early.

**Clause 3 (who gave it).** A dose recorded from another provider is an entry that names no Kestrel store; a dose Kestrel gave at one of its stores is an entry that names a Kestrel store.

### Interval thresholds by vaccination

A dose comes too early when the days after the earlier dose are fewer than the minimum interval less the grace period days. A dose given exactly on the threshold day is not too early.

| Vaccination | Dose 2 minimum interval | Dose 3 minimum from dose 2 | Dose 3 minimum from dose 1 | Grace period days | Too early when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seasonal Influenza Standard-Dose Vaccination | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 | never (the thresholds fall below zero) |
| Seasonal Influenza High-Dose Vaccination | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 | never |
| COVID-19 Updated Vaccination | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 | never |
| RSV Older Adult Vaccination | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 | never |
| Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccination | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 | never |
| Recombinant Zoster Two-Dose Series | 56 | 0 | 0 | 4 | dose 2 fewer than 52 days after dose 1 |
| Hepatitis B Three-Dose Series | 28 | 56 | 112 | 4 | dose 2 fewer than 24 days after dose 1; dose 3 fewer than 52 days after dose 2, or fewer than 108 days after dose 1 |

### Entries taken off

| Latest dose came too early | Who gave it | Entries taken off |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Recorded from another provider | 1 |
| Yes | Kestrel, at one of its stores | 2 (the dose and the registry copy of Kestrel's report of it) |
| No | either | 0 |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

- Recombinant Zoster Two-Dose Series, dose 2 given 51 days after dose 1: 51 is fewer than 56 less 4, which is 52, so it came too early. At 52 days it did not.
- Hepatitis B Three-Dose Series, dose 2 given 23 days after dose 1: too early (the threshold is 28 less 4, which is 24). At 24 days it is not.
- Hepatitis B Three-Dose Series, dose 3 given 60 days after dose 2 and 107 days after dose 1: the dose 2 test is met (60 is not fewer than 52), but 107 is fewer than 112 less 4, which is 108, so it came too early. At 108 days after dose 1 and 52 or more after dose 2 it did not.

### Worked example (hypothetical)

A Hepatitis B Three-Dose Series course's latest entry is dose 2, given 20 days after dose 1 at a Kestrel store. 20 is fewer than 24, so it came too early, and Kestrel gave it: 2 entries are taken off. Had the same dose 2 been an entry recorded from another provider, 1 entry would be taken off; had it been given 30 days after dose 1, none would be.
